body: The former Mission Mall site in Mission, Kansas, a 17-acre tract known as Mission Gateway that has sat empty for about 20 years, is headed to a sheriff's sale. Metropolitan Commercial Bank sued owner Aryeh Realty LLC, a New York company that the Johnson County Post identified as a subsidiary of the Cameron Group, in 2023, saying Aryeh failed to repay about $24 million on a $26 million loan dating to 2019. In December 2025, after closing arguments on Dec. 9, Johnson County District Court Judge Robert Wonnell granted the bank's request to proceed with a foreclosure sale while other legal issues were resolved, the Post reported.

On Friday, Oct. 2, 2026, the court entered a final judgment requiring Aryeh to pay $46.24 million for the loan default and unpaid property taxes and gave it until Oct. 16 to pay before the bank could request a sale by the Johnson County Sheriff, KCTV5 reported. After the deadline passed, the bank's attorney filed the request on Monday, Oct. 26, and in court documents filed Friday, Oct. 30, a judge ordered the sheriff's sale, according to KCTV5. No sale date had been announced.

In early October, the City of Mission announced an agreement with the R.H. Johnson Company that "contemplates the acquisition of the former Mission Mall site," KCTV5 reported. That agreement depends on the outcome of the foreclosure proceedings.

timeline.label: Metropolitan Commercial Bank makes a $26M loan on the Mission Gateway site
Metropolitan Commercial Bank sues Aryeh Realty LLC over the defaulted loan in Johnson County District Court
Judge Robert Wonnell hears closing arguments and grants the bank's request to proceed with a foreclosure sale
Court enters a $46.24M final judgment for the loan default and unpaid property taxes
Payoff deadline for Aryeh Realty passes
Bank's attorney asks the court for a sheriff's sale
Court orders a sheriff's sale of the property; no sale date set
